location.quote: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents that share a memory must decide which agent to ask

findings.observed: The routing problem and its cost (global search consults every candidate on every query) are stated in the first sentence and reinforced in Section 1. Minor friction: the problem is framed for 'teams', but the tested corpus has two agents, and 'candidates' (32.0 per query) are clearly not agents, so the unit being searched is unclear.
findings.reader_struggle: The reader grasps the problem immediately but has to reconcile 'which agent to ask' with a candidate set of 32 when there are only two agents.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers may picture routing among many agents and overestimate the scale of the problem actually studied.
findings.revision_principle: State the problem at the scale actually tested and define the unit of search (agent versus memory item) when the problem is introduced.

location.quote: The authors give a reason for foregrounding cost and answerability rather than answer accuracy as the primary measures.

findings.observed: The paper refers to the authors' reason for prioritising cost over accuracy but never says what it is. It also does not argue why a per-query saving matters in practice: global search uses about 180 tokens per query, so the saving is about 40 tokens.
findings.reader_struggle: An adjacent-field reader cannot judge whether token cost is the right primary measure, or whether 40 tokens per query matters at deployment scale.
findings.likely_consequence: The reader may regard the headline as statistically solid but practically unmotivated, or suspect accuracy was demoted to protect the result.
findings.revision_principle: When a design choice is justified by a reason, give the reason where it is invoked, and link the cost measure to a realistic operating scale.

location.quote: RQ1: how many fewer LLM tokens per query does routing to a learned owner use than global search

findings.observed: Four explicit RQs plus a boundary check, each answered in a subsection whose heading matches it. RQ4 ('how does ... behave') does not name its criterion (cumulative regret in route@1) until Section 3.4.
findings.reader_struggle: Little struggle. RQ4 is open-ended until the reader reaches the method.
findings.likely_consequence: The questions are clear. RQ4's success criterion is learned late.
findings.revision_principle: Name the measurable criterion inside each research question.

location.quote: we claim no novelty: no literature search was run for this draft.

findings.observed: The contributions are honestly tied to results, but with no related work an expert cannot tell what is new about ownership-based routing. Contribution 5 counts correcting a stored statistic as a contribution. The objective says the paper 'presents ASMOS', yet the system gets two short paragraphs.
findings.reader_struggle: Specialist readers cannot place the work. Some listed contributions are bookkeeping, not findings.
findings.likely_consequence: The reader sees the paper as an internal evaluation report of uncertain novelty, not as a system contribution.
findings.revision_principle: Keep contributions to findings a reader can reuse, and position them against prior work, or say explicitly that the contribution is a bounded measurement.

location.quote: Ownership of a topic is learned online from verification-gated reputation: a verified claim raises an agent's ownership

findings.observed: Core mechanics are missing. What a 'claim' is and who or what verifies it; how a query's topic is determined; whether ownership is learned before the 50 evaluation queries or during them (possible leakage); what a 'candidate' is; how the ownership update rule works; and what the 10 seeds randomise at temperature 0.
findings.reader_struggle: An adjacent-field reader cannot reconstruct the method, and a specialist cannot check whether the evaluation queries also trained ownership.
findings.likely_consequence: The reader accepts the numbers but cannot tell what produced them or whether the setup favours A1.
findings.revision_principle: Specify the learning signal, the update rule, the train/evaluate separation and the source of randomness before reporting results that depend on them.

location.quote: Ownership frozen at its initial prior (A2) is the single-variable ablation of A1: the router falls back to global search.

findings.observed: A2 never routes and is effectively global search by construction (route@1 0.0). Even so, its tokens (179.3) and candidate-set size (31.7) differ slightly from A0 (180.2, 32.0) without explanation, and it is not said why the prior ownership times similarity always falls below tau.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers have to work out that the ablation is degenerate, and cannot explain the small A0/A2 differences.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers may overread the ablation as isolating the learning process rather than 'routing versus no routing'.
findings.revision_principle: When an ablation collapses to another arm, say so explicitly and explain any residual differences.

location.quote: which the authors regard as a degraded offline mode and not the evaluation baseline, so routing results use MiniLM.

findings.observed: Which embedder is used where is inconsistent. 'Routing results use MiniLM', yet the new-topic runs use all-mpnet-base-v2 and bge-m3, and the cost run's embedder is 'unconfirmed'. The classifier baselines give identical results under both embedders, so the reader cannot tell what features they use.
findings.reader_struggle: The reader cannot map embedders to experiments.
findings.likely_consequence: Confusion about which configuration produced the headline, and doubt about whether the classifiers are a fair comparison.
findings.revision_principle: Give one explicit mapping from each experiment to its embedder and baseline features.

location.quote: the classifier baselines use a threshold of 0.5 and are either frozen, retrained every 5 steps, or retrained every 10 steps

findings.observed: ASMOS's threshold (0.351493) was tuned on the same corpus, while the classifiers use an untuned 0.5. There is no online-updated classifier baseline, even though ASMOS consumes the same 10 labels. The number of agents in the new-topic regime is not given. With 5 queries per step, per-seed route@1 moves in steps of 0.2.
findings.reader_struggle: A specialist cannot judge whether the comparison is fair or only shows the retraining schedule.
findings.likely_consequence: The regret advantage may be read as algorithmic when it could reflect tuning and update-frequency asymmetry.
findings.revision_principle: Match baselines on tuning budget and label or update access, and include the strongest simple baseline for the same information.

location.quote: The evaluation set has 50 queries in five query classes on a corpus with two agents

findings.observed: The cost experiment is small (50 queries, two agents, asymmetry by construction). The five query classes are never described, and the accuracy grading is undocumented (Section 6.1 says an LLM grades). The separability check reports 'go' without its criterion.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot judge how representative the queries are, or whether results differ by query class.
findings.likely_consequence: The design reads as a proof-of-concept whose results may depend on how the corpus was built.
findings.revision_principle: Describe the query classes and grading procedure, and report results by class when the classes differ in kind.

location.quote: over 48 non-zero pairs of 50; the rank-biserial correlation is r = 0.941 (T+ = 1141.5, T- = 34.5)

findings.observed: Results are precise and internally consistent: T+ + T- = 1176 = 48*49/2, and r = (T+ - T-)/1176 = 0.941. The per-query win/tie/loss counts are given. Minor friction: context tokens are presented as 10-seed means in 4.1, but Section 3.2 says context tokens exist only for seeds 66 to 110.
findings.reader_struggle: Little. A verifier has to reconcile which columns cover which seeds.
findings.likely_consequence: The headline is understood and credible. There is small uncertainty about the seed basis of the secondary numbers.
findings.revision_principle: Label the seed basis of every reported quantity where it appears.

location.quote: since the only difference between A1 and A2 is whether ownership updates

findings.observed: The interpretation is hedged ('consistent with', 'low confidence'), which is good. But the ablation contrasts routing with no routing, because A2 falls back to global search. It cannot separate ownership evolution from any above-threshold ownership, for example a correctly set static ownership.
findings.reader_struggle: Specialists see that the ablation's reach is narrower than its framing; others accept the framing.
findings.likely_consequence: Non-specialists may believe the learning process itself was shown to produce the saving.
findings.revision_principle: Interpret an ablation only by the contrast it actually creates, and name the alternative explanations it leaves open.

location.quote: ASMOS-memory used 353.7 total tokens per question against 711.4 for RAG but scored lower

findings.observed: ASMOS-memory scored below the no-memory baseline (token-F1 0.4155 against 0.5642) while using more tokens. The paper does not discuss this: it implies the memory injects harmful context, which could also bear on the accuracy shortfall of A1.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers are left to ask why adding memory hurts and whether the same mechanism explains A1's lower accuracy.
findings.likely_consequence: A surprising negative is registered but not understood.
findings.revision_principle: When a system underperforms a trivial baseline, give at least a bounded account of why, and link it to related findings.

location.quote: Additional caveats are ours, not the authors' concessions.

findings.observed: The limitations are unusually thorough and specific: missing files, threshold tuned in-sample, undocumented grading, embedder dependence, single runs. Missing items: only two agents; the token accounting excludes the cost of verification and ownership updates; seeds at temperature 0 may not be independent replications. The unbounded accuracy cost is not respected in the Conclusion.
findings.reader_struggle: A mixed audience gets an honest picture, apart from the omitted scale and cost-accounting caveats.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers trust the disclosure but may still generalise beyond two agents and overlook hidden costs.
findings.revision_principle: List every condition that bounds the headline claim, including scale and cost-accounting scope, and make downstream summaries obey them.

location.quote: Whether that reason holds on this corpus is an open question to the authors, so we do not adopt it

findings.observed: The paper uses two voices: 'the authors state' and 'we'. Sections 6.1 and 6.2 separate 'the authors' concessions' from 'ours'. It reads like a third party reporting on someone else's project, with phrases such as 'material available to us' and 'result file not in the material'.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot tell who ran the experiments, who stands behind each claim, or why the writers lack the authors' files.
findings.likely_consequence: Confusion about authorship and responsibility for the claims, and weaker trust.
findings.revision_principle: Use one consistent authorial voice and attribute claims to their evidence, not to parties.

location.quote: under a frozen memory contract (version 1.2) with a six-stage lifecycle from new to forgotten

findings.observed: Several terms are well defined inline (route@1, regret, global search, A0 to A3). Others are used without explanation: 'memory contract', 'six-stage lifecycle', 'verification-gated reputation', 'claim', 'topic', 'candidate', 'transactive', 'go' for the separability check, and 'centerpiece run'. Answerability gets one vague clause.
findings.reader_struggle: An adjacent-field reader meets project jargon that does not help understanding and cannot tell which terms matter.
findings.likely_consequence: Cognitive effort spent on irrelevant terms, and fuzzy understanding of the ones that matter (claim, topic, candidate, answerability).
findings.revision_principle: Define every term the results depend on at first use, and remove project-internal labels that the argument does not need.

location.quote: The effect size is the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation .

findings.observed: The audience is stated not to know this statistic. The paper justifies choosing it but never says what it measures (the normalised difference between positive and negative rank sums) or how to read r = 0.941.
findings.reader_struggle: The target reader cannot interpret the effect size, only accept it.
findings.likely_consequence: The effect size becomes a number without meaning to the target audience.
findings.revision_principle: When a statistic is new to the intended audience, give its meaning and scale before its justification.

location.quote: Section 2 gives context, Section 3 the setup, Section 4 the results by question

findings.observed: The structure mirrors the RQs, and each results subsection ends by saying what it answers and what it does not. Section 4.6 (the statistics correction) comes after the static-QA boundary, although it concerns 4.1.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers of 4.1 do not know that its effect size was revised until two subsections later.
findings.likely_consequence: Minor: the flow is good overall.
findings.revision_principle: Place corrections next to the result they correct.

location.quote: The first five seeds come from an earlier result file that is not in the material available to us

findings.observed: Half the headline seeds come from an unavailable file with an unconfirmed embedder. The route@1 denominators are unstated: 0.909 and 0.614 imply 40/44 and 27/44, not 50 queries. The criterion for 'routed the new topic in 5 of 5 seeds' is undefined. The corpus, queries and code are unavailable.
findings.reader_struggle: A verifier can check internal arithmetic but cannot trace several numbers to their denominators or sources.
findings.likely_consequence: The reader trusts the direction of the results but cannot independently verify the headline or route@1.
findings.revision_principle: Give the denominator and source for every reported proportion, and state which results rest on unavailable data.

location.quote: Route@1 on the new topic by step

findings.observed: In Figure 3, the horizontal axis is labelled 'Route@1 on the new topic' with ticks 0.00 to 1.00, but horizontal position actually encodes step 0 to 10. Route@1 is carried on the vertical axis, which has no ticks or label. Figures 1 and 2, by contrast, are clear: the non-zero axis is disclosed and the CI is shown.
findings.reader_struggle: A reader who uses the axis labels reads step as route@1 and cannot read route@1 values at all.
findings.likely_consequence: The key RQ4 figure is misread or unreadable without the caption and text.
findings.revision_principle: Label each axis with the quantity its position encodes, with ticks and units, and check the axes against the data mapping.

findings.observed: For ASMOS + RAG, exact match (0.625) exceeds token-F1 (0.4329). That is impossible if an exact match scores F1 = 1 on the same predictions. The note that exact match equals 'the containment scores in every row' suggests the column is really containment. The caption stresses token-F1, where the combined system looks much worse than RAG, while its exact-match gap to RAG is small (0.625 against 0.708).
findings.reader_struggle: A verifier finds the table inconsistent with standard metric definitions and cannot tell which metric to trust.
findings.likely_consequence: Doubt about the static-QA results and about how carefully the metrics were computed.
findings.revision_principle: Define each metric precisely, check that reported values satisfy the metrics' logical relations, and summarise tables across all metrics shown.

location.quote: at a small accuracy cost in every measured seed

findings.observed: Section 4.2 says 'the size of the accuracy cost cannot be bounded' (no paired test, undocumented grading), yet the Discussion and Conclusion call it 'small'. Most other claims (22.1%, the CI, 'consistent with') are aligned with their evidence.
findings.reader_struggle: A reader who reads only the conclusion gets a stronger reassurance than the results allow.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers believe the accuracy cost is known to be small.
findings.revision_principle: Carry each result's stated uncertainty unchanged into the summaries.

location.quote: ASMOS found a new topic with no retraining and lower regret than scheduled classifiers

findings.observed: The regret superiority rests on 5 seeds, with no significance test, undocumented classifier tuning, asymmetric thresholds, and no online-updated baseline. Elsewhere: 'higher answerability (0.909 versus 0.727)' comes from a single run with no query count, and 'more queries to the correct owner than similarity alone' has no test, where chance with two agents is about 0.5.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot tell which comparisons are established and which are descriptive.
findings.likely_consequence: Descriptive differences are read as demonstrated advantages.
findings.revision_principle: Report untested comparisons as observations in the tested run, and state fairness conditions before ranking methods.

location.quote: The authors state that more seeds cannot narrow a confidence interval that is set by heterogeneity between queries

findings.observed: Several points appear three or four times: the seed/interval argument, the constructed corpus, and 'not a QA-accuracy method' appear in 4.x, 5, 6 and 7. The Discussion's first paragraph restates the RQ answers. The repetition mostly reinforces scope and is not badly harmful.
findings.reader_struggle: Mild fatigue. Readers may skim the limitations and miss the new caveats among the repeats.
findings.likely_consequence: New caveats in 6.2 get less attention.
findings.revision_principle: State each caveat once where it bounds a result, and have the limitations section add only what is not already bounded.

location.quote: its N can be read three ways (0.803, 0.819 or 0.568 on the headline)

findings.observed: The text carries many numbers and much over-precision (22.0911%, tau = 0.351493, 0.2666 and 0.1024 centroids), statistics trivia (alternative effect sizes, Pratt versus wilcox, the correction record), and long parenthetical qualifications. Tables and figures help.
findings.reader_struggle: Adjacent readers lose the thread among numbers that do not change any conclusion.
findings.likely_consequence: The main message is harder to extract, and readers may skip the method.
findings.revision_principle: Keep in the main text only the numbers that support a claim, at a precision that matches their uncertainty, and move audit detail aside.

location.quote: 4.1 RQ1: routing to a learned owner cut tokens per query by 22.1%

findings.observed: The results headings state the finding and name the RQ. The roadmap is explicit, and each subsection ends with 'This answers RQn' plus what it does not show. The abstract mostly stands alone and defines regret and route@1 inline, but uses 'answerability' and 'verified outcomes' undefined.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers always know where they are. The abstract has two undefined terms.
findings.likely_consequence: Good navigation. A mixed reader of the abstract alone misreads answerability.
findings.revision_principle: Make the abstract self-sufficient by defining every measure it reports.

location.quote: learned ownership is a candidate way to lower per-query token cost

findings.observed: The takeaway is stated and correctly scoped, but its practical weight is not. 39.8 tokens per query on a 180-token budget is not translated into when it matters, whether it scales with memory size, or how it compares with the uncounted costs of verification and ownership updates.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot decide whether to care about the saving in their own setting.
findings.likely_consequence: The finding is remembered as '22% cheaper' without a sense of whether that is worth an accuracy loss.
findings.revision_principle: Translate the effect into the reader's decision: the conditions under which it is worth adopting, and the full cost ledger.

inference_issues.claim_text: routing ... used 22.1% fewer LLM tokens per query than global search, at a small accuracy cost in every measured seed
inference_issues.missing_link: Section 4.2 says the size of the accuracy cost cannot be bounded (no paired test, undocumented grading), so 'small' is not supported. The same wording appears in Section 5 ('where ... a small accuracy cost is acceptable').

inference_issues.claim_text: routing kept answerability but lowered accuracy in every measured seed
inference_issues.missing_link: At temperature 0 the seeds are nearly deterministic (the per-seed token spread is 0.07 points), so the five seeds are not independent replications. The difference is 1 to 2 of 50 questions under an undocumented LLM grader, with no paired test, so even the direction is weakly supported.

inference_issues.claim_text: With ownership frozen at its initial value the saving nearly disappeared, which is consistent with ownership evolution producing it
inference_issues.missing_link: A2 falls back to global search by construction, so the contrast is routing versus no routing. There is no arm with static but informative ownership, no test, and a threshold tuned on the same corpus, so the ablation cannot single out the evolution process.

inference_issues.claim_text: ASMOS found a new topic with no retraining and lower regret than scheduled classifiers
inference_issues.missing_link: 5 seeds, no significance test, classifier tuning undocumented, ASMOS threshold tuned in-sample while the classifiers use 0.5, and ASMOS consumed the same 10 labels. Budget parity is unverified.

inference_issues.claim_text: the classifier baselines ... are either frozen, retrained every 5 steps, or retrained every 10 steps
inference_issues.missing_link: There is no classifier updated online from the same labels ASMOS uses, which is the natural like-for-like baseline. The comparison shows the retraining schedule as much as the method.

inference_issues.claim_text: The primary measure is LLM total tokens per query
inference_issues.missing_link: The token accounting covers the answering call only. The costs of producing verification outcomes, updating ownership and embedding are not reported, so the net saving is unknown.

inference_issues.claim_text: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents that share a memory must decide which agent to ask
inference_issues.missing_link: The cost corpus has two agents, and the new-topic regime's agent count is not stated. There is no evidence about larger teams.

inference_issues.claim_text: ASMOS with the MiniLM-L6-v2 embedder matched the classifier on route@1 (1.0 versus 1.0) with higher answerability (0.909 versus 0.727)
inference_issues.missing_link: This is a single run with no seeds and no stated query count. The values suggest 11 queries, which would be a two-query difference, and there is no test.

inference_issues.claim_text: The route@1 of A1 was 0.909 against 0.614 for A3, so learned ownership sent more queries to the correct owner than similarity alone
inference_issues.missing_link: No test is reported, and the denominator is unstated (the values imply 44 queries, not 50). With two agents, chance route@1 is about 0.5.

inference_issues.claim_text: combining ASMOS with RAG does not recover RAG's token-F1
inference_issues.missing_link: The caption emphasises token-F1, where the combined system trails RAG by 0.32. On exact match it trails by only 0.08 (0.625 against 0.708), and exact match exceeding token-F1 for that row points to a metric definition or computation problem that goes unaddressed.

inference_issues.claim_text: these counts are exact usage figures ... and do not depend on the embedder, while the embedder of their earliest centerpiece run is unconfirmed
inference_issues.missing_link: The counting method does not depend on the embedder, but the counted quantity does: routing and candidate-set size depend on similarity. Pooling seeds 11 to 55 from a missing file with an unconfirmed embedder is therefore not made safe by this argument.

objective_discrepancies: The objective says the paper presents ASMOS as a shared semantic memory with a learned ownership layer; the paper conveys a measurement study and describes ASMOS's mechanism only thinly (verification source, update rule and topic assignment are not specified).
The objective says the saving 'came with a small accuracy cost'; the paper's own results section says the size of the accuracy cost cannot be bounded, so 'small' is not what the evidence conveys.
The objective frames ASMOS for 'teams of LLM agents'; the paper tests a two-agent corpus, which the reader learns only in Section 3.2.

The objective says ASMOS 'adapted without retraining'; the paper conveys this, but also that ASMOS consumed as many labels as the retrained classifiers, so a reader may wrongly infer adaptation without supervision.
The objective's points on how certain the saving's size is and which conclusions are not supported are conveyed well and match the reconstruction.
